subject: Intermittent 429 surge during batch ingestion — affinity/rate binding suspected

From: Rajesh Singh <rajesh@medicai.com>

Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Spike of 429s during nightly ingestion — urgent

Hi Dylan / Marissa,

We saw a big spike of 429s starting around 02:00 UTC during our nightly batch ingestion window. The job retries generated a retry storm and downstream queueing — several downstream consumers timed out. Attached are a sample of the ingestion logs and a short call trace from our side.

This started after your team’s tiering changes last week (we were moved to the "preferred-tier" binding). Our SPOC Ops are seeing: 30–40% 429s for short bursts (~3–7 minutes) and overall call latency increased by ~250ms. This is impacting our SLA for ingest success rate.

Can you confirm whether any rate affinity binding or project-to-org rate mapping changed? We need a short triage and a mitigation plan (can we increase allowance or route to a lower-affinity pool?)

Thanks — Rajesh

Subject: Re: Spike of 429s during nightly ingestion — urgent

On Tue, May 4, 2027 at 02:15 AM Rajesh Singh <rajesh@medicai.com> wrote:
> We saw a big spike of 429s starting around 02:00 UTC during our nightly batch ingestion window.

Quick infra findings (initial):
- The tiering cutover did a project->affinity rebind but a subset of MedicaI's worker projects kept an older rate-policy tag (rate-bound-affinity=legacy) which caused their tokens to be evaluated against a smaller per-project bucket.
- Traffic skew: ~65% of ingestion requests were concentrated on two identical host pools due to a sticky affinity rule (we accidentally kept a host-affinity preference flag set during the rollout).
- Result: transient saturation on those pools causing the 429s and promoting retries from client side into a visible retry storm.

Planned mitigations (immediate):
1) Manual lift: Increase the per-project soft quota for the affected projects by 3x for the next 6 hours (done at 04:10 UTC).
2) Rebind: Remove the legacy rate-policy tag and reassign 50% of workers to an alternate affinity pool to spread the ingestion traffic (in progress).
3) Short-term traffic shaping: Apply a 2s retry-debounce policy at the gateway for MedicaI projects to dampen client-side retry amplification.

I'll follow up with exact host IDs and request ids. We expect error rate to fall in the next 20–30 minutes after the rebind finishes.

Ava Chen
Infra Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
ava_chen@redwood.com

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Rajesh Singh <rajesh@medicai.com>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike of 429s during nightly ingestion — postmortem and next steps

Rajesh — following up after the mitigation. Summary: the manual lift + rebind completed; 429s returned to baseline within ~18 minutes and overall tail latency improved. We attached a short SLA impact summary.

Root cause (concise): during the tiering cutover a legacy rate-policy tag (rate-bound-affinity=legacy) remained set for a subset of MedicaI project IDs. That tag caused those projects to be evaluated against a smaller per-project bucket and, combined with a persistent host-affinity preference, concentrated traffic on two identical pools. The combined effect produced transient saturation and client retry amplification.

Fixes enacted:
- Removed legacy tag from all MedicaI project IDs and validated rebind mapping.
- Added a pre-deploy validation to detect legacy rate-policy tags during future cutovers.
- Added a temporary automatic debounce policy we can enable per-org when sustained spikes are detected.

Customer impact: estimated 6.4k failed requests during the 27-minute window (we've included traces). We will follow Redwood's incident policy and process a service credit equivalent (we recommend 5% of the affected month) — Marissa, can you confirm credit line to the account?

Rajesh, we're available for a 30-min wrap-up call if you'd like. Very sorry for the disruption.

Evelyn Hart
Sr. Infra Lead, Redwood Inference
